title: What becomes of with_force_64bit, the test-only u64 build?
body:
`SuffixArrayBuilder::with_force_64bit` (`libsufr/src/build.rs:154`) is `pub(crate)` under `cfg(test)`. It makes a build of a small text write u64 integers, so the u64 construction path can be tested without a 4 GiB input. The one caller is the unit test at `lib.rs:270`, which reads the result through `TypedSuffixArray::<u64>::open` directly, because the public `open_with` picks the width from `text_len` and would read the file as u32. The format has no width field, which is sufr-fde85d.

So the hook writes files the format cannot describe, and the u64 path is tested only inside the crate: the integration oracle in `libsufr/tests/oracle.rs` runs at u32 only.

## Options

| option | what it gives | cost |
|---|---|---|
| keep it as it is | the one unit test | the oracle never sees u64 |
| record the width in the header (sufr-fde85d), then make the hook public | the oracle runs every row at both widths through the public API, and a user can make u64 files on purpose | the format change |
| delete it | one less test-only path in the builder | no u64 test at all short of a 4 GiB input |
